questions.question: Which of the following peaks is NOT located in the Himalayan mountains?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalsubai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kalsubai is the highest peak in Maharashtra, located in the Western Ghats.
 
• It is not a part of the Himalayan mountain range.
 
• The peak stands at an elevation of 1,646 meters (5,400 feet) above sea level.
 
• Kalsubai is situated in the Ahmednagar district and is a popular trekking destination.
 
• The other peaks listed (Nanda Devi, Kamet, and Annapurna) are all located in the Himalayan mountains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nanda Devi**

 
 
• It is the second highest mountain in India, located in the Garhwal Himalayas in the state of Uttarakhand.
 
• It stands at an elevation of 7,816 meters (25,643 feet).
 
• Nanda Devi is part of the Nanda Devi National Park, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Kamet**
 
 
• Kamet is the second highest mountain in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand, India.
 
• It has an elevation of 7,756 meters (25,446 feet).
 
• Kamet is part of the Zanskar Range in the Himalayas.
 
 
 
• **Annapurna**
 
 
• Annapurna is a mountain massif in the Himalayas located in north-central Nepal.
 
• It includes one peak over 8,000 meters—Annapurna I Main, which stands at 8,091 meters (26,545 feet).
 
• The Annapurna Conservation Area is the largest protected area in Nepal.

questions.question: India's total length of coastline of the mainland including Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep is __________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7516.6 km**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's total length of coastline of the mainland including Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep is **7,516.6 kilometers.**
 
• This includes the mainland coastline of 6,100 kilometers, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands coastline of 1,900 kilometers, and the Lakshadweep Islands coastline of 160 kilometers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India's coastline is one of the longest in the world, and it is home to a variety of coastal ecosystems, including beaches, mangroves, coral reefs, and estuaries.
 
• These ecosystems provide important habitat for a wide range of plants and animals, and they also play a vital role in the Indian economy.

questions.question: The _______ plateau is sub-divided into the Garo Hills, the Khasi Hills, and the Jaintia Hills, named after the tribal groups inhabiting the region.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya**__.

__
 
• **The Meghalaya plateau is sub-divided into the Garo Hills, the Khasi Hills, and the Jaintia Hills, named after the tribal groups inhabiting the region**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meghalaya Plateau:**

 
 
• The plateau is separated from the main block of the peninsular plateau by a gap called the **Garo-Raj Mahal gap.**
 
• From east to west, the plateau comprises Garo Khasi, Jaintia and Mikir hills.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chottanagpur Plateau**

 
 
• It is composed mainly of Gondwana rocks with patches of granites and gneisses and Deccan lavas.
 
• It covers mostly Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Purulia of West Bengal. 
 
 
 
• **Central Highland:**
 
 
• The Central Highland lies to the north of the Narmada River covering a major area of the Malwa Plateau.
 
• The Aravalli range is surrounded by the central highlands in the north-west and the Vindhya range in the south.

questions.question: Why will a person weigh more at the north or south pole?

options.text: Due to Earth’s distance from the sun
Due to variation in centrifugal force of earth with latitude
Due to variation in centripetal force of earth with altitude
Due to variation in centripetal force of earth with latitude

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Due to variation in centrifugal force of earth with latitude**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The centrifugal force on Earth is caused by its rotation and is strongest at the equator due to the higher rotational velocity.
 
• At the poles, the centrifugal force is negligible as the poles do not experience the same rotational velocity as the equator.
 
• Less centrifugal force at the poles reduces the outward "push," causing a person to weigh more compared to their weight at the equator.
 
• Earth’s shape, which is slightly oblate (flattened at the poles and bulging at the equator), also contributes to the variation in weight.
 
• The gravitational force is slightly stronger at the poles due to the reduced distance from the Earth’s center compared to the equator.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Centrifugal Force:** A pseudo-force that acts outward on a mass when it is rotating, proportional to the rotational velocity and the radius of rotation.
 
• **Earth’s Shape:** The Earth is an oblate spheroid; it is flatter at the poles and bulges at the equator, influencing gravity and centrifugal forces.
 
• ** Gravity is slightly stronger at the poles because they are closer to the Earth’s center compared to the equator.
 
• Weight vs Mass:** Weight is the force exerted due to gravity and varies with location, while mass remains constant regardless of location.
 
• **Rotational Impact:** Earth’s rotation affects the distribution of centrifugal force, which contributes to the difference in apparent weight across latitudes.

questions.question: Which of the following is the smallest Union Territory of India in terms of area?

options.text: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lakshadweep.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Lakshadweep is the smallest union territory of India and its total surface area is just 32 km2.
 
• Lakshadweep is an archipelago of 36 islands in the Arabian sea, located 200 to 440 km off of the mainland's southwestern coast.
 
• In Malayalam, Lakshadweep means "One lakh islands".
 
• Malayalam is the official as well as the widely spoken native language in the territory.
 
• Kavaratti is the capital of the Union Territory Lakshadweep in India. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goa** is the smallest state** **in India, in terms of its area.
 
• **Sikkim** is the smallest state in India as per population.
 
• **Rajasthan** is the largest state in India by area.
 
• **Uttar Pradesh** is the largest state in India in terms of population.

questions.question: India accounts for what percent of total geographical area of the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **2.4 percent**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India accounts for approximately 2.4 percent of the total geographical area of the world. 
 
• India is the seventh-largest country in the world in terms of geographical area.
 
• It is situated in South Asia.
 
• India shares its borders with Pakistan to the northwest, China and Nepal to the north, Bhutan to the northeast, and Bangladesh and Myanmar to the east. To the south, it is bounded by the Indian Ocean.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Geographically, India is extremely diverse, featuring a wide range of climate regions and landscapes.
 
• Here are some of the main geographical features:
 
 
• **The Himalayas: **
 
• This mountain range in the north serves as a natural barrier between India and the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• Mount Kanchenjunga, located on the border between India and Nepal, is the highest point in India.
 
• **The Northern Plains:**
 
• Also known as the Indo-Gangetic Plains, this region was formed by the basin of the Indus, Ganga (Ganges), and Brahmaputra rivers.
 
• It's one of the world's most fertile and densely populated areas.
 
• **The Thar Desert:**
 
• Located in the northwestern part of India, it's the world's 17th largest desert and the ninth largest subtropical desert.
 
• **The Deccan Plateau:**
 
• This large plateau in southern India is elevated and characterized by rolling hills and valleys.
 
• **The Ghats: **
 
• The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats are mountain ranges that run parallel to India's western and eastern coasts, respectively.
 
• **Coastal Plains:**
 
• India has extensive coastal plains on both its eastern and western coasts.
 
• The western coastal plains are narrower, while the eastern coastal plains are broader and more fertile.
 
• **Islands: **
 
• India has two major island groups – the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal and the Lakshadweep Islands in the Arabian Sea.

questions.question: In its longitudinal extent, the Himalaya consists of ______ parallel ranges.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __three.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Himalayas consist of three main parallel ranges, namely **The greater Himalayas, The lesser Himalayas, and The outer Himalayas**.
 
• The** northernmost range of the Himalayas** is known as the Great Himalayas.
 
 
• It is also called Himadri.
 
• Himadri is the backbone of the Himalayas.
 
• It is the most continuous range consisting of the loftiest peaks with an average height of 6,000 metres.
 
• It contains all the prominent Himalayan peaks like Mount Everest, Annapoorna, Nandadevi, etc.
 
 
 
• The Lesser Himalayas is the** mountain range that lies between Himadri and Siwali**k.
 
 
• It is also called Himachal.
 
• It is mainly composed of highly compressed and altered rocks.
 
• The altitude varies between** 3,700 and 4,500 metres and the average width is 50 Km.**
 
• Pir Panjal is the largest range in Himachal.
 
• This region is well known for its hill stations.
 
 
 
• The **outermost range of the Himalayas** is called the Shiwalik(Outer Himalayas.)
 
 
• It extends over a width of 10-50 Km and has an altitude varying between** 900 and 1100 metres**.
 
• The word Shiwalik literally means** "tresses of Shiva".**
 
• **Shiwalik is parallel to the Ganga plain.**

questions.question: Which among the following is not a part of Western Ghats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahadeo Hills.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Mahadeo Hills are a range of hills in Madhya Pradesh state of central India.
 
• These are located in the northern part of the Satpura Range.
 
• Highest peak is Dhoopgarh.
 
• Satpura Mountain Range is southward of Vindhya Hills and parallel to it.
 
• Mahadeo Hills are located in Gujarat.
 
• Satpura range is a range of hills in Central India.
 
• The range rises in eastern Gujarat, through the border of Maharashtra and Madya Pradesh to the east of Chhattisgarh.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__The Western Ghats:__

 
• Also called the *Sahyadri*, the Western Ghats are a north-south chain of mountains that mark the western edge of the Deccan plateau region.
 
• **They rise abruptly from the coastal plain of the Arabian Sea as an escarpment of variable height, but their eastern slopes are much more gentle.**
 
• The horizontally bedded lavas due to weathering have given a characteristic ‘landing stair aspect’ to the relief of this mountain chain.
 
• Contain a series of residual plateaus and peaks separated by saddles and passes.
 
• Mahabaleshwar, located on a laterite plateau, is one of the highest elevations in the northern half, rising to 1,430 m.
 
• The chain attains greater heights in the south, where the mountains terminate in several uplifted blocks bordered by steep slopes on all sides, Those include the:
 
• Nilgiri Hills, with their highest peak, Doda Betta (2,637 m).
 
• the Anaimalai, Palni, and Cardamom hills**, all three of which radiate from the highest peak in the Western Ghats, Anai Peak (Anai Mudi (2,695 metres)).**

questions.question: Which of the following minerals are NOT found in Chota nagpur-belt?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Chota Nagpur Plateau** is very rich in **minerals** and **precious stones**.
 
• Some of the important minerals found here include **coal, iron ore, asbestos, chromite, mica, and kyanite**. **The Indo-Gangetic plains** are poor in mineral deposits.
 
• It covers Jharkhand, the northern part of Chhatisgarh, and the Purulia district of West Bengal.
 
• This plateau is composed mainly of Gondwana rocks.
 
• The Damodar valley has vast coal reserves, and the Hazaribagh region is one of the main sources of mica in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mysore Plateau

 
 
• The name of the plateau is derived from Karnad (“Land of Black Soil”).
 
• The Karnataka Plateau is composed of ancient volcanic rocks, crystalline schists, and granites of the Precambrian age.
 
• There are large reserves of iron ore in the Baba Budan hills and gold in the Kolar Gold Fields.
 
 
 
• Deccan Plateau
 
 
• The Deccan Plateau is a large plateau in western and southern India.
 
• Primary mineral ores found in this region are mica and iron ore in the Chhota Nagpur region, and diamonds, gold, and other metals in the Golconda region.
 
 
 
• Malwa Plateau
 
 
• The Malwa Plateau roughly forms a triangle based on the Vindhyan Hills, bounded by the Aravali Range in the west and Madhya Bharat Pathar to the north, and Bundelkhand to the east.
